lessons.title: Cloud storage and collaborating on a project

steps.title: Why collaborating in the cloud is smarter
steps.body: Instead of texting or emailing a document back and forth, tools like Google Docs, Sheets, or Word Online let you work in the same file at the same time as others. Changes show up instantly, and you can see who changed what — ideal for group work.

steps.title: Version history: your lifesaver before a deadline
steps.body: Accidentally deleted or overwritten something right before submitting? Via File > Version history (Google Docs) you can view and restore an earlier version. No more need to keep separate backup files.

steps.title: Organizing folders smartly
steps.body: Use shared folders for projects you work on with others, and keep your personal files separate. Consistent naming (date + subject) saves you a lot of searching later.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Create a new document in Google Drive below and check out the sharing and version-history options.

lessons.title: Backing up and securing your phone

steps.title: Setting up automatic backup
steps.body: Turn on automatic backup for photos, contacts, and app data (Android: Settings > System > Backup; iPhone: Settings > [your name] > iCloud). This way you don't lose all your photos and chats if your phone breaks or gets stolen.

steps.title: Finding or wiping your phone remotely
steps.body: Turn on 'Find My Device' (Android) or 'Find My iPhone' (Apple). If lost or stolen (at a festival or a night out, say), you can use this to see its location, make it ring, or remotely wipe all data.

steps.title: Screen lock and updates
steps.body: Use a PIN, pattern, or biometric lock — never 'no lock', even if you trust your housemates or friends. Install software updates as soon as possible: they often close security gaps.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Check on your own phone whether automatic backup and 'find my phone' are turned on.

lessons.title: The subscription jungle: getting a grip on Spotify, Netflix & co.

steps.title: Creeping subscription costs
steps.body: Spotify, Netflix, Disney+, cloud storage, a gym app, gaming subscriptions — it adds up faster than you think. Periodically (every quarter, say) review your bank statement for recurring payments you no longer use.

steps.title: Sharing without the drama
steps.body: Sharing a family or duo plan with housemates or friends is cheaper, but agree upfront on who pays when (via a payment request app, for example) — that avoids later arguments about 'who still owes that last €3'.

steps.title: Free trials: always set a reminder
steps.body: A 'free trial month' that automatically converts into a paid subscription is a classic trap. Set a reminder in your calendar or phone right when you sign up, so you cancel on time if you don't want to keep it.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Check your active subscriptions in your phone's settings (or app store account) and see if there's anything you no longer use.

lessons.title: Making a password manager a daily habit

steps.title: Why this should be a habit by now
steps.body: As we saw in the Safety module: a password manager isn't an extra step anymore, it's a basic habit — like locking your screen. It remembers, generates, and auto-fills your passwords, for every app and account you have.

steps.title: Everything in one place
steps.body: Besides passwords, a password manager often lets you store bank details, ID documents, and secure notes — encrypted, and accessible only with your master password.

steps.title: Sharing with housemates or family
steps.body: Most password managers offer a family or group plan that lets you securely share passwords (like a streaming account), without literally texting the password in the group chat.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: If you don't use a password manager yet: install one today and set it up for your most important account.
